title: Crossy Road
statementMd:
Lucky Lab A is west of Guadalupe Street, while Lucky Lab B is east of it. There are $n$ loyal customers of Lucky Lab A waiting on the east sidewalk and $m$ loyal customers of Lucky Lab B waiting on the west sidewalk. Customer $i$ of Lucky Lab A is at vertical position $a_i$, and customer $i$ of Lucky Lab B is at vertical position $b_i$. Multiple customers may begin at the same position.

Before crossing, every customer may walk along their current side of the street to any integer vertical position. They then cross Guadalupe in a straight horizontal line. Customers traveling in the same direction may cross together, but a customer heading west and a customer heading east cannot use the same vertical position, or they would collide.

Walking from vertical position $x$ to vertical position $y$ costs $|x-y|$. Find the minimum possible total walking cost that lets everyone cross without a collision.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $n$ and $m$ ($1\le n,m\le 2000$) — the number of customers loyal to Lucky Lab A and Lucky Lab B, respectively.

The second line contains $n$ integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$ ($1\le a_i\le n+m$) — the starting vertical positions of the customers loyal to Lucky Lab A.

The third line contains $m$ integers $b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_m$ ($1\le b_i\le n+m$) — the starting vertical positions of the customers loyal to Lucky Lab B.

## Output

Output a single integer — the minimum possible total walking cost.

## Note

In the first sample, all three Lucky Lab B customers walk vertically to position $2$ on their side, then cross. The Lucky Lab A customers at positions $1$ and $3$ cross without moving, while the customer starting at position $2$ walks to position $1$ before crossing. The total cost is $3$.

In the second sample, one customer must walk one unit before crossing because customers traveling in opposite directions cannot both cross at position $1$.
